messages:
devon: heads up — console quota tiles are showing inflated per-route usage after the routing-catalog change yesterday. looks like analytics is still joining on the old route_id field so we get duplicates for aliased routes. anyone on quick sync?

anna: ugh. saw that in the dashboards. is this the route aliasing we added for prefix-based routing?

devon: yes. new policy introduces route_alias table + route_id_alias column. ingest writes alias metadata but analytics join still expects canonical route_id. result: same logical route appears under multiple ids in console metrics.

sam: quick proposal: add a routing_catalog_v2 table with (canonical_route_id, alias_id, canonical_since) and dualwrite both catalog versions at ingest for 2 weeks. analytics can read catalog_v2 for joins and fall back to v1 if missing.

maria: dualwrite + read-fallback sounds ok but backfill cost could be huge. how many routes? ~1.2M route ids, 95% small tenants. need an incremental backfill plan not single big job.

lee-enginfra: +1 for incremental. we should run a cursored backfill that writes compact parity rows to catalog_v2 in chunks and emits progress to our migration topic. keep batch_size small to avoid DB spikes.

anna: for safe reads, can we add a local read-adapter where console queries use COALESCE(c2.canonical_route_id, c1.canonical_route_id) so we can flip a feature flag per-service? less risky than switching all joins at once.

devon: good call. plan: 1) add catalog_v2 + indirection; 2) write read-adapter using COALESCE; 3) dualwrite ingest for 14d; 4) background backfill phased by tenant; 5) switch console to prefer v2; 6) remove v1 after 30d.

sam: need a canary plan. pick 10 low-traffic tenants + internal staging to validate. we'll compare console vs raw telemetry (token-level counts) and set alerts for >1% divergence.

maria: backfill implementation notes: idempotent SQL: 
```
INSERT INTO routing_catalog_v2 (canonical_route_id, alias_id, canonical_since)
SELECT canonical_route_id, alias_id, now()
FROM routing_catalog_v1
WHERE alias_id > :cursor_start AND alias_id <= :cursor_end
ON CONFLICT (alias_id) DO NOTHING;
```
Run in 5000-row windows, commit per window. emit progress to migrations.kv topic.

lee-enginfra: add a migration flag in the console config: `routes.catalog_read_pref = ["v2","v1"]` so we can flip order without deploy chaos. Also add a timeout fallback to skip heavy joins.

devon: telemetry changes: we need to add `route_catalog_version` to ingest events and to console traces so we can measure how many rows are served from v2 vs v1. small change to ingest schema and to trace envelope.

anna: can we avoid a heavy analytic backfill by adding a short-term query-time enrichment: join against a materialized mapping cache (Redis) filled by incremental backfill job? That reduces load on analytics DB during migration cutover.

sam: redis cache helps for reads, but analytics historical aggregates still need correct keys for time-series. we should do the incremental backfill on the analytics denorm tables for the recent 90 days first, then historical cold data later.

maria: agree. prioritise last 90 days for backfill window. older windows can be recalculated offline or left behind if stale is acceptable for >1y. we need cost estimate for recompute.

devon: action items: @anna add read-adapter PR and feature flag; @maria author backfill runner with cursor + progress topic; @sam define canary tenant list and divergence alert; @lee-enginfra add config flag + short-circuit timeout; i'll update the migration doc and schedule a canary deploy next wed.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — feature-flag-service v2 -> staging (id: ff-202) :rocket:

anna: I'll start the PR and tag reviewers. keeping canary window to 48h. if anyone sees dashboards go weird, ping me in #eng-platform asap. :thumbsup:
